title: The situation in Veloria
summary: Security Council crisis in a fictional state: ceasefire, aid access, an arms embargo, sanctions and a UN mission. Every position is invented for practice.

committee.name: Security Council: the situation in Veloria (demo)
committee.conference: Evatt-style practice: the situation in Veloria (demo)
committee.notes: Fictional scenario for practice. Council membership as remembered for 2026; check before use.

topic.name: The situation in Veloria (fictional demo scenario)
topic.notes: Fictional demo scenario. Every country position is invented and labelled Unverified demo.

tags.peacekeeping: Authorises a UN mission under Chapter VII
tags.accountability: Sets up an independent commission of inquiry

preambular.text: Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Veloria,
Expressing grave concern at the deteriorating humanitarian situation in the eastern provinces of Veloria and the displacement of civilians,
Welcoming the mediation efforts of the regional organisation and encouraging all parties to engage with them in good faith,

operative.text: Demands that all parties to the conflict in Veloria immediately cease hostilities and observe a nationwide ceasefire;
Calls upon all parties to allow and facilitate the safe, rapid and unimpeded passage of humanitarian relief to all civilians in need;
Decides that all Member States shall prevent the direct or indirect supply, sale or transfer of arms and related materiel to Veloria for twelve months;
Decides that all Member States shall impose travel bans and asset freezes on individuals designated by the Committee as obstructing the peace process;
Authorises, acting under Chapter VII of the Charter, the deployment of a United Nations stabilisation mission to protect civilians in the eastern provinces;
Requests the Secretary-General to establish an independent commission of inquiry into alleged violations of international humanitarian law in Veloria;

news.headline: Ceasefire collapses in the eastern provinces
news.body: Fighting has resumed near the river town of Marrow Ford after a two-day pause. Both sides blame the other for the first shot. Aid agencies have suspended convoys.

news.headline: Aid convoy stopped at a checkpoint
news.body: A twelve-truck food and medicine convoy has been held at a checkpoint for nine hours. Local officials say paperwork is incomplete; aid workers say the delay is deliberate.

news.headline: Regional mediators offer talks in a neutral capital
news.body: The regional organisation proposes face-to-face talks within ten days, on condition that the Council does not impose new sanctions meanwhile.

news.headline: Reports of weapons crossing the northern border
news.body: Satellite images published by an independent research group appear to show armoured vehicles crossing into Veloria. The images have not been verified.

news.headline: Refugee numbers double in a week
news.body: Neighbouring states report that more than 80,000 people have crossed from Veloria in seven days. One neighbour has asked the Council for emergency funding.

news.headline: Both sides agree to a 72-hour humanitarian pause
news.body: The parties will hold fire for three days to let aid through, if the Council guarantees independent monitors. The offer expires at midnight.

cards.text: Welcomes the offer of regional mediators and urges all parties to attend talks in good faith, with the Council to review progress after thirty days;
Urges all parties to observe a pause in fighting of seventy-two hours so that aid can pass, to be extended if monitors confirm it is respected;
Demands that all parties give independent monitors immediate access to every checkpoint on aid routes and allow convoys to pass without delay;
Decides that the arms embargo shall apply to armed groups outside government control, and shall be reviewed after six months;
Requests the Secretary-General to send unarmed civilian monitors, with the consent of Veloria's government, to observe the ceasefire and the movement of aid;
Encourages the regional organisation, with United Nations support, to set up an inquiry led by Velorian and regional jurists into alleged violations;
Decides that targeted sanctions shall be suspended while the parties take part in talks, and shall be restored if the talks are abandoned;
Calls upon neighbouring States to keep their borders open to civilians and requests donors to give emergency funding to the States hosting them;

events.title: A convoy reaches Marrow Ford
events.body: After a long delay, a convoy of aid trucks is waved through the checkpoint and arrives at Marrow Ford. Delegates ask how to make sure the next one is not stopped.
events.teaches: Small steps on the ground can show what is possible, and diplomats use them as a base for firmer agreements.

events.title: Veloria's government writes to the Council
events.body: A letter from Veloria's government says it will accept outside observers if it keeps a say in who they are and where they go. Delegations read it closely.
events.teaches: A State's consent is central to how the UN works, and many missions only go ahead because the host State agrees.

events.title: Independent researchers confirm the border images
events.body: The research group that published the border images says experts have now checked them. Delegates debate what the Council should do with confirmed information.
events.teaches: Reliable evidence changes diplomatic debates, which is why checking facts before acting is such an important habit.

events.title: The regional organisation briefs delegates
events.body: Representatives of the regional organisation visit the Council corridors and explain what a neutral capital could offer. They warm to those who ask about their plan.
events.teaches: Regional bodies know the parties well, and the UN often works alongside them rather than in their place.

events.title: Capitals ask for new instructions
events.body: Several delegations say their capitals are still reviewing the latest news, so side talks take longer to arrange this turn.
events.teaches: Diplomats act on instructions from home, so they cannot always agree to a change at once, even when they want to.

events.title: A respected mediator briefs the Council
events.body: A senior mediator with long experience of peace talks speaks to the Council and answers questions. Her calm manner is noted by many delegates.
events.teaches: Respected mediators help parties find common ground, because both sides can trust a person who is not seen as taking sides.

author: Ben Gough and the build session (D-063)
